title: Android
blurb: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, lifecycle, MVVM and offline-first data, WorkManager, testing, performance, security and Play publishing.

quiz.question: Which survives configuration changes but NOT process death?
quiz.explanation: Persist important data in Room/DataStore; keep small UI state in SavedStateHandle.

quiz.question: What does a sealed interface give you in Kotlin when modelling UI state?
options: Exhaustive when expressions checked by the compiler
quiz.explanation: The compiler ensures every state is handled.

quiz.question: Why provide a key in LazyColumn items?
options: Stable identity so Compose can update, move and preserve item state efficiently
quiz.explanation: Keys avoid unnecessary recomposition and state mix-ups.

quiz.question: In an offline-first architecture, what does the UI observe?
options: The local database as the single source of truth
quiz.explanation: The repository writes network data into Room; UI observes Room Flows.

quiz.question: Which API is right for a guaranteed, deferrable photo upload that must survive app restarts?
quiz.explanation: WorkManager persists work with constraints and retries.

quiz.question: What do Baseline Profiles improve?
options: Startup and runtime performance via ahead-of-time compilation of critical paths

quiz.question: Where should a privileged backend API secret live?
options: On the server, never in the app
quiz.explanation: Anything in the APK can be extracted.

quiz.question: What does a staged rollout let you do?
options: Release to a small percentage, monitor crash-free users and ANRs, and halt if needed
quiz.explanation: It limits blast radius of regressions.

problems.title: Offline-first menu screen
problems.prompt: Design an Android menu screen that works on patchy networks.
problems.solution: Room DAO Flow observed via repository; refresh writes network data into Room; ViewModel combines flows into StateFlow UiState with refresh/error flags; show cached data with offline banner; queue writes via WorkManager with constraints; test with fakes and process-death scenarios.
